done_when: A Not-done finding that matches the item's Done-when with small wording changes (missing or extra small words, case, punctuation) still blocks; a Not-done finding about builder details stays a follow-up

known.title: Functional: Reworded Done-when findings still become follow-ups
Functional: Distinct outcomes become the same normalized words

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a reviewer inserts “also” into an otherwise matching finding, such as “The guide lists the commands and the worker brief also carries them.” The filter removes only six specific small words, so this finding does not match the approved sentence without “also”. Punctuation changes inside words also fail: “The e-mail is sent to users” and “The email is sent to users” produce different word sequences. In both cases, close classifies the unmet outcome as a follow-up. The new test covers an extra “the” and punctuation between words, so it does not catch these cases.
Done when: A Not-done finding that matches the item's Done-when with small wording changes (missing or extra small words, case, punctuation) still blocks; a Not-done finding about builder details stays a follow-up
findings.title: Functional: Reworded Done-when findings still become follow-ups

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an approved outcome says “The form shows the name of the owner”, while a reviewer requests the builder detail “The form shows the name to the owner in bold”. Removing both “of” and “to” makes the approved words a prefix of the detail, so close treats the unapproved formatting and audience requirement as a blocking Done-when finding. Significant symbols also collapse: “Build a C++ client” and “Build a C client” normalize identically. These are different outcomes that become identical ordered sequences, which the ordered-word ruling did not address.
findings.title: Functional: Distinct outcomes become the same normalized words

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a reviewer rewords an approved story-task outcome, or an earlier-adopted repo closes a review saved before upgrading. Every new proof case starts a fresh fix, although story tasks obtain their approved items through a separate path in src/forge/review.py:1078, and saved reviews are reclassified at src/forge/close.py:290. Existing task and upgrade tests use exact wording. The proof would therefore still pass if reworded task findings or saved pre-upgrade findings remained non-blocking. Exercise both cases through forge close.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_small_word_changes_block_but_builder_details_stay_follow_ups

why: A Not-done finding about the item's own Done-when becomes a non-blocking follow-up when the reviewer rewords the Done-when slightly (#1493)
